idiom_name: NamedTuple/tuple nodes + one evaluate() using match/case
implementation_notes: Since 3.10 the language has structural pattern matching, so the AST can be plain data (dataclasses, NamedTuples or tuples) and evaluation one recursive function with match/case: class patterns deconstruct by attribute or position and dataclasses supply __match_args__ automatically. This is the default when several operations will walk the same tree, because the nodes stay values and each pass is a separate function; use the class-per-node form when a rule's validation and semantics belong next to its data.
code_sketch:
from typing import NamedTuple
class Num(NamedTuple):
    value: int
class Add(NamedTuple):
    left: object
    right: object
def evaluate(expr, ctx):
    match expr:
        case Num(value): return value
        case Add(left, right): return evaluate(left, ctx) + evaluate(right, ctx)
        case _: raise EvalError(f'unhandled node: {expr!r}')
pitfalls: Sequence and class patterns match duck-typed shapes, so a node with the wrong arity or attribute names falls into the catch-all; make the catch-all raise, never return a default.
A NamedTuple (or a frozen dataclass) compares and hashes by value, so large subtrees are compared element-wise when used as dict keys - key such tables by id() or opt out of value equality.
Recursive evaluate() hits Python's recursion limit; raise it only together with an explicit depth bound on the input, or a small expression can exhaust the stack.

variants.name: Class per grammar rule with an evaluate method
variants.idiom_name: ABC/Protocol Expression + one class per rule implementing eval(context)
variants.implementation_notes: The GoF shape in Python: an abstract base (abc.ABC or a typing.Protocol) declaring the interpret/evaluate operation and one class per grammar rule, recursing through child attributes. It keeps constructor validation and a rule's semantics together, works on every supported Python 3, and is easy to extend with a new node class. Once a third operation must walk the same tree, the operations multiply across all classes and data nodes plus match (or a visitor) becomes the better structure.
pitfalls: ABCs reject instantiation only for methods marked abstractmethod; Protocol conformance is structural and checked by type checkers, so a misspelled method fails at call time.
isinstance-based dispatch inside the evaluator reintroduces exactly the fragility the classes were meant to remove; let the node own its rule.
Mutable node attributes make the tree a shared mutable object: two evaluations over the same tree interfere unless the nodes are treated as read-only.
